title: Tag System
story: You're building a photo app. Every photo can have tags like 'sunset', 'beach', 'friends'. You need a way to add tags, remove tags, and quickly check 'does this photo have the tag nature?' — without duplicates. Enter the Set.
why: Sets store unique items and check membership instantly — perfect for tags, permissions, categories, and any collection where duplicates are meaningless.
analogy: A Set is like a VIP guest list — you're either on it or you're not. Adding your name twice doesn't put you on the list twice. The bouncer only checks 'are you on the list?' and the answer is a simple yes or no.
try_it: Add a `remove_tag` function and a `count_tags` function that returns the number of tags. Then build a `merge_tags` function that takes two Photos and returns a new Set containing tags from both. For a challenge: create a function that finds photos matching ALL given tags (not just any).
tips: `.contains(&value)` instantly checks membership — no loop needed, unlike Vec
`.insert(value)` on a Set silently ignores duplicates — it's safe to insert the same tag twice
Use Set when you care about 'is this item in the collection?' — use Vec when you care about order or count
common_mistakes: Using `.len()` to check membership — O(n) loop vs O(1) with `.contains()`
Confusing Set.remove with Vec.pop — Set.remove needs a specific value: `tags.remove(&"beach")`
Expecting Set to maintain insertion order — Sets prioritize fast lookups over ordering
